newsitem.title: USA: Homeless advocate Cuomo pegged for housing chief.
newsitem.headline: Homeless advocate Cuomo pegged for housing chief.

text.p: Andrew Cuomo brings to President Bill Clinton's cabinet a famous political pedigree and a passionate belief in helping the homeless and poor.
Cuomo was tapped on Friday to head up the Department of Housing and Urban Development, where he has been an assistant secretary for community planning and development for more than three years.
The 39-year-old Cuomo is a political insider as the son of former New York Gov. Mario Cuomo and the husband of Kerry Kennedy, a daughter of the late Sen. Robert Kennedy.

Cuomo is said to have vaulted to the top of the list to replace outgoing HUD Secretary Henry Cisneros on the strength of a recommendation from Vice President Al Gore after Cuomo helped Gore to prepare for the vice presidential debate against Jack Kemp.

As assistant secretary, Cuomo has strived to help the poor by championing the so-called Empowerment Zone programme, which aims to create jobs and provide work training. He also has worked to increase funding for the homeless.
Cuomo grew up on politics, as his father spent 12 years as governor of New York. The elder Cuomo was known worldwide as one of the Democratic Party's most articulate and eloquent speakers.
His father once said Andrew Cuomo's first job in politics was "putting my posters up and pulling the other guy's down."
One of Mario and Matilda Cuomo's five children, Andrew Cuomo once joked to a New York Times interviewer that "the greatest burden you carry being the son of Mario Cuomo is his nose."
Cuomo's name also had been mentioned lately as a possible challenger to New York Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato in 1998.
He attended Fordham University and Albany Law School and practiced law as assistant district attorney in Manhattan and as a partner in the firm of Blutrich, Falcone and Miller.
He also worked as his father's campaign manager and strategist and special assistant to the governor of New York.
In 1986, he founded H.E.L.P., which grew to be the largest private provider of transitional housing for the homeless in the United States.
In 1991 Cuomo was named to lead the New York City Commission on the Homeless, the youngest commission chairman in city history.
Cuomo and his wife Kerry, the seventh of Robert and Ethel Kennedy's 11 children, have twin two-year-old daughters, Cara Ethel and Mariah Matilda.

He and his wife, a human rights activist, are often named as one of Washington's so-called power couples. Time magazine once wrote a tongue-in-cheek list of such couples, referring to the pair as "Not much fun but great last names."
